ei.title: The Power of the First Ten Minutes
ei.subject: 올림포스전국연합고1_2026

fullPassage: Inefficient teachers overlook the potential power of the opening minutes of class. Often, if students are quiet enough and if there are many pressing demands on a teacher's time at that moment, more than ten minutes can disappear before class starts. It's no wonder that students are late for class; they have little reason to be on time. You can use the first ten minutes to get your class off to a great start, or you can choose to waste this time. The first minutes set the tone for the rest of the class. If you are prepared for class and have taught your students an opening routine, they can use this brief time to make mental and emotional transitions from the last class or subject and prepare to focus on learning new material. In summary, you should establish an opening routine to develop your class with an effective start.

It's no wonder that students are late for class; they have little reason to be on time. You can use the first ten minutes to get your class off to a great start, or you can choose to (C)[waste / save] this time. The first minutes set the tone for the rest of the class. If you are prepared for class and have taught your students an opening routine, they can use this brief time to make mental and emotional transitions from the last class or subject and prepare to focus on learning new material. In summary, you should establish an opening routine to develop your class with an effective start.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) overlook=간과하다, (B) disappear=사라지다, (C) waste=낭비하다
det.analysis:
❌ ① notice — disappear — waste: (A) notice(알아차리다)는 overlook(간과하다)과 반대 의미
❌ ② overlook — remain — waste: (B) remain(남다)은 disappear(사라지다)와 반대
✅ ③ overlook — disappear — waste: 원문 일치. 비효율적 교사는 수업 시작의 힘을 간과하고(overlook), 10분이 사라지며(disappear), 시간을 낭비(waste)한다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ④ overlook — disappear — save: (C) save(아끼다)는 waste(낭비하다)와 반대
det.tip: overlook the power / minutes can disappear / choose to waste this time

questions.passage: Inefficient teachers overlook the (A)[limited / potential] power of the opening minutes of class. Often, if students are quiet enough and if there are many (B)[trivial / pressing] demands on a teacher's time at that moment, more than ten minutes can disappear before class starts. It's no wonder that students are late for class; they have little reason to be on time. You can use the first ten minutes to get your class off to a great start, or you can choose to waste this time. The first minutes set the tone for the rest of the class. If you are prepared for class and have taught your students an opening routine, they can use this brief time to make mental and emotional transitions from the last class or subject and prepare to focus on learning new material. In summary, you should (C)[establish / abandon] an opening routine to develop your class with an effective start.

❌ ② limited — pressing — establish: (A) limited(제한된)는 potential(잠재적)과 다른 의미
❌ ③ potential — trivial — establish: (B) trivial(사소한)은 pressing(긴급한)과 반대
❌ ④ potential — pressing — abandon: (C) abandon(버리다)은 establish(확립하다)와 반대
det.tip: potential power / pressing demands / establish an opening routine

det.korean: set: (A) 찻잔 한 벌/세트(명사) / (B) 분위기를 설정하다/조성하다(동사)
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 놓다 — (B) 설정하다: (A)는 '놓다'가 아닌 명사 '세트/한 벌'
✅ ② (A) 세트/한 벌 — (B) 설정하다/조성하다: (A)는 찻잔 한 벌(a tea set), (B)는 첫 몇 분이 분위기를 설정한다는 뜻으로 다의어의 두 의미를 올바르게 연결 ←정답
❌ ③ (A) 세트/한 벌 — (B) (해가) 지다: (B)의 set은 분위기를 설정하는 것이지 해가 지는 것이 아님
❌ ④ (A) 정해진 — (B) 굳어진: (A)는 형용사가 아닌 명사, (B)도 '굳어진'이 아닌 동사
det.tip: set: ① (명사) 세트/한 벌 ② (동사) 설정하다/조성하다 ③ (동사) (해가) 지다 ④ (형용사) 정해진

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a sequence of actions regularly or usually followed"

det.korean: routine=일과/루틴 (정기적으로 따르는 일련의 행동)
det.analysis:
✅ ① routine(일과/루틴): 정기적으로 따르는 일련의 행동이라는 영영 정의에 정확히 일치 ←정답
❌ ② demand(요구): 무언가를 요청하는 것으로 정의와 불일치
❌ ③ transition(전환): 한 상태에서 다른 상태로의 이동으로 정의와 불일치
❌ ④ material(자료): 가르치거나 배우는 내용으로 정의와 불일치
det.tip: routine = 정기적으로 반복되는 일과/루틴

questions.passage: The first minutes set the tone for the rest of the class. They can use this brief time to make mental and emotional __________ (transition) from the last class or subject.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: make 뒤의 목적어로 복수 명사 transitions 사용
det.analysis: 'make mental and emotional transitions'에서 두 형용사(mental, emotional)의 수식을 받는 복수 명사가 필요. 여러 종류의 전환을 가리키므로 복수형 transitions가 적절. transition → transitions
det.tip: make transitions = 전환을 만들다 (복수형)

questions.passage: If you are prepared for class and have taught your students an opening routine, they can use this brief time well. In summary, you should establish an opening routine to develop your class with an __________ (effect) start.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: 명사 effect를 형용사 effective로 변환 (명사 start 수식)
det.analysis: 관사 an과 명사 start 사이에 명사를 수식하는 형용사가 필요. 명사 effect(효과)를 형용사 effective(효과적인)로 바꿔야 한다. effect → effective
det.tip: effect(명사, 효과) → effective(형용사, 효과적인). an effective start

questions.passage: Inefficient teachers overlook the potential power of the opening minutes of class. Often, if students are quiet enough and if there are many pressing demands on a teacher's time at that moment, more than ten minutes can disappear before class starts. It's no wonder that students are late for class; they have little reason to be on time. You can use the first ten minutes to get your class off to a great start, or you can choose to waste this time. The first minutes __________ for the rest of the class. If you are prepared for class and have taught your students an opening routine, they can use this brief time to make mental and emotional transitions from the last class or subject and prepare to focus on learning new material. In summary, you should establish an opening routine to develop your class with an effective start.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: set the tone=분위기를 설정하다 — 첫 몇 분이 나머지 수업의 분위기를 설정한다는 맥락
det.analysis:
❌ ① break the rule(규칙을 어기다): 분위기 설정 맥락과 무관
❌ ② lose the point(요점을 놓치다): 맥락과 불일치
❌ ③ miss the chance(기회를 놓치다): 분위기 설정과 다른 의미
✅ ④ set the tone(분위기를 설정하다): 원문 일치. 첫 몇 분이 나머지 수업의 분위기를 설정한다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
det.tip: The first minutes set the tone — 첫 몇 분이 분위기를 설정한다

questions.passage: Inefficient teachers overlook the potential power of the opening minutes of class. Often, if students are quiet enough and if there are many pressing demands on a teacher's time at that moment, more than ten minutes can disappear before class starts. It's no wonder that students are late for class; they have little reason to be on time. You can use the first ten minutes to get your class off to a great start, or you can choose to waste this time. The first minutes set the tone for the rest of the class. If you are prepared for class and have taught your students an opening routine, they can use this brief time to make mental and emotional transitions from the last class or subject and prepare to __________. In summary, you should establish an opening routine to develop your class with an effective start.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: focus on learning new material=새로운 자료 학습에 집중하다 — 전환 후 새 내용 학습에 집중하도록 준비한다는 맥락
det.analysis:
❌ ① leave the classroom early(교실을 일찍 떠나다): 학습 준비 맥락과 반대
✅ ② focus on learning new material(새로운 자료 학습에 집중하다): 원문 일치. 전환을 만들고 새로운 자료 학습에 집중하도록 준비한다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ③ repeat the previous lesson(이전 수업을 반복하다): 새 내용 학습 맥락과 불일치
❌ ④ ignore the daily schedule(일정을 무시하다): 맥락과 무관
det.tip: prepare to focus on learning new material — 새 자료 학습에 집중하도록 준비하다
